issues.root_cause: No _sanitize_text or equivalent function was implemented; text reaches provider dispatch with raw file paths, URLs, and hashes intact. The test expects these to be replaced with safe placeholders. This is a privacy/security gap that exists across ALL providers, not specific to local_http.
issues.impact: One test failure; sensitive paths could leak to external TTS APIs
issues.fix: Implement a text sanitization step in text_to_speech_tool() before the provider dispatch if/elif chain: replace absolute paths, well-known audio extensions, URLs, and hex hashes with safe placeholders (e.g. 'a file path', 'an audio file', 'a link', 'a hash'). The test at tests/tools/test_tts_local_http.py:135 can serve as the specification.

verification.git_status: All changes are UNCOMMITTED modifications. test_tts_local_http.py is untracked.
verification.root_cause: The original bug was that `elif provider == 'local_http'` never existed, so when provider was set to local_http the code fell through to the Edge TTS default else-block, calling Edge while still logging `provider: local_http`. The fix adds the dispatch branch and adds an unknown-provider guard so explicit-but-unknown providers error instead of falling through.
